pages.text: Heat is a state function, so the heat of any reaction can be added up from steps already measured (Hess). The $(item)Heat-Pack Reactor$() runs reactions for their heat: ammonia and nitric acid neutralise to $(item)Ammonium Nitrate$(), giving heat out - mixed too fast it runs away. Dissolving it again takes heat in: $(fluid)Cold Pack Solution$() at 268 K. Salt and ice make $(fluid)Eutectic Brine$() at 252 K.
Both cold packs are $(thing)coolants$(): pour them into a physics machine's coolant loop to hold it below room temperature - colder than water, though they carry less heat.
